classification.difficultyReason: Complete the square, interpret the resulting shifts and reflection, then connect the vertex and exact intercepts to each sketch; distinguish the quadratic with no real roots.

content.prompt: Complete the square and so use shifting to help sketch the graph of each quadratic function. Indicate the vertex and all intercepts with the axes.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2+2x+1-1+3\\y&=(x+1)^2+2\end{align*}$$
Shift $y=x^2$ left 1 unit and up 2 units. The vertex is $(-1,2)$.
$$\begin{align*}y\big|_{x=0}&=3\end{align*}$$
Since $(x+1)^2+2\ge2$, there are no $x$-intercepts.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2-4x+4-4+1\\y&=(x-2)^2-3\end{align*}$$
Shift $y=x^2$ right 2 units and down 3 units. The vertex is $(2,-3)$.
$$\begin{align*}(x-2)^2-3&=0\\(x-2)^2&=3\\x-2&=\pm\sqrt3\\x&=2\pm\sqrt3\\y\big|_{x=0}&=1\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upward parabola with vertex (2,-3), exact root labels staggered across the axis, and y-intercept 1.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(x^2-2x)+2\\y&=-\big((x-1)^2-1\big)+2\\y&=3-(x-1)^2\end{align*}$$
Reflect $y=x^2$ in the $x$-axis, then shift right 1 unit and up 3 units. The vertex is $(1,3)$.
$$\begin{align*}3-(x-1)^2&=0\\(x-1)^2&=3\\x&=1\pm\sqrt3\\y\big|_{x=0}&=2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Downward parabola with vertex (1,3), exact roots and y-intercept 2.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2-x+\frac14-\frac14-1\\y&=\left(x-\frac12\right)^2-\frac54\end{align*}$$
Shift $y=x^2$ right $\tfrac12$ unit and down $\tfrac54$ units. The vertex is $(\tfrac12,-\tfrac54)$.
$$\begin{align*}\left(x-\frac12\right)^2-\frac54&=0\\\left(x-\frac12\right)^2&=\frac54\\x-\frac12&=\pm\frac{\sqrt5}{2}\\x&=\frac{1\pm\sqrt5}{2}\\y\big|_{x=0}&=-1\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upward parabola with fractional vertex, exact radical roots and y-intercept -1. Enlarged to separate labels.
